patches.value: Let D=dim_H(E), F=E×[0,1]. First show 0≤D≤n<∞. Nonnegativity is part of the critical-exponent definition. If n=0, ℝ⁰ is a singleton and E is that singleton, so D=0. If n>0, compactness H002 implies boundedness: the open cover of E by radius-one balls has a finite subcover, so E lies in a bounded box. For every sufficiently small h>0, subdivide this box into at most C h^(−n) grid cubes, C independent of h, each of diameter ≤√n h. For every fixed m>n their total m-power diameter cost is at most C n^(m/2)h^(m−n)→0. M008's scale-cover formula therefore gives H^m(E)=0 for every m>n, whence D≤n by the critical-exponent definition. Fix arbitrary q>D; q>0. M003 at the NNReal coercion of q gives H^q(E)=0. Unfold M008: this is the supremum over positive scales of the infimum cover cost, so every scale content C_q(E,r)=0. To ensure the admissible cover class is nonempty at any r>0, cover E by open balls of radius r/3 and use compactness to take a finite subcover; these sets have diameter ≤2r/3, and appending empty sets makes a Nat-indexed r-cover. Thus for every r>0 and γ>0 the infimum definition supplies a Nat-indexed r-cover of cost <γ. Choose r_j↓0, r_j≤1, and γ_j↓0 with covers of cost <γ_j. Each nonempty zero-diameter member in Euclidean space is a singleton. Enumerate these by a finite or countable list and replace the k-th by an open ball containing it, of diameter ≤r_j and q-power cost <γ_j2^(−k−1); total added cost is <γ_j. Leave positive-diameter members and empty members unchanged. The resulting cover has all nonempty diameters d_i positive, d_i≤r_j, and q-cost <2γ_j. For each i partition [0,1] into N_i=⌈1/d_i⌉ closed intervals of length 1/N_i≤d_i; since d_i≤1, N_i≤1/d_i+1≤2/d_i. The products U_i×K_iℓ cover F, have diameter ≤√2d_i, and form a countable family (a countable union of finite families), which can be enumerated by ℕ with empty sets appended. Their total (q+1)-cost is at most 2(√2)^(q+1)∑d_i^q<4(√2)^(q+1)γ_j, tending to zero; their diameters are ≤√2r_j→0. M008 gives H^(q+1)(F)=0; M012 at NNReal exponent q+1 gives dim_H(F)≤q+1. Since this holds for every q>D, density gives dim_H(F)≤D+1. For n=0, F is isometric to [0,1]; interval covers of mesh tending to zero have total a-cost tending to zero for every a>1, so H^a(F)=0 and M012 gives dim_H(F)≤1=D+1. Isometries preserve ediam, cover conditions, and the exact M008 formula.

For each i, if B_i is nonempty, choose an open interval J_i containing B_i whose length is at most ediam(B_i)+η_i≤ρ_i+η_i, by enlarging its infimum/supremum enclosure by total width η_i. If B_i is empty, choose any open interval of length η_i; it still contains B_i and has length ≤ρ_i+η_i.
Use the two real endpoints of the closed interval enclosure of J_i∩[0,1]; M011 evaluates the volume of that interval as ofReal(right endpoint minus left endpoint), bounded by ofReal(ρ_i+η_i).

For D>0 fix 0<s<D. For a>0 define C_a(A,δ)=inf{∑'ᵢ ediam(Uᵢ)^a : U:ℕ→Set(X), A⊆⋃ᵢUᵢ and ∀i ediam(Uᵢ)≤δ}. Empty members have diameter zero and hence zero cost. In M008, the supremum over nonempty witnesses is the ordinary power for a nonempty member and zero for the empty member; thus its inner infimum is exactly this content and H^a(A)=sup_{δ>0}C_a(A,δ), with no normalization factor. If δ₁≤δ₂, every δ₁-admissible cover is δ₂-admissible, so C_a(A,δ₁)≥C_a(A,δ₂). The one-sided limit as scale decreases to zero therefore equals this supremum. M001 gives H^s(E)=∞; hence C_s(E,δ)→∞, meaning that for every finite K all sufficiently small positive δ have C_s(E,δ)>K. Fix δ>0 and any countable δ-cover (Vᵢ) of F. Set ρᵢ=ediam(Vᵢ), Aᵢ=π₁(Vᵢ), Bᵢ=π₂(Vᵢ). Coordinate projections are 1-Lipschitz in the concatenated Euclidean metric, so diam(Aᵢ),diam(Bᵢ)≤ρᵢ≤δ. Given ε>0 set ηᵢ=ε2^(−i−1)/(1+ρᵢ^s)>0. If Bᵢ is nonempty it is bounded; extend its infimum/supremum enclosure by total width ηᵢ to obtain open Jᵢ⊇Bᵢ of length ≤ρᵢ+ηᵢ. If Bᵢ is empty choose any open interval of length ηᵢ; it contains Bᵢ and meets the same length bound. For every t∈[0,1] and x∈E, (x,t) lies in some Vᵢ, so x∈Aᵢ and t∈Bᵢ⊆Jᵢ. Therefore the Aᵢ with t∈Jᵢ cover E at scale δ. The definition of infimum gives C_s(E,δ)≤∑'ᵢ1_{Jᵢ∩[0,1]}(t)ρᵢ^s pointwise for t∈[0,1]. Put ν=volume.restrict([0,1]) on ambient Borel ℝ. For integration on all ℝ multiply the left side by 1_[0,1]; outside [0,1] it is zero, and ν is supported on [0,1], so the resulting inequality holds ν-a.e. Every Jᵢ∩[0,1] is Borel; its indicator multiplied by ρᵢ^s is measurable and AEMeasurable for ν. The ambient total mass is ν(ℝ)=volume([0,1])=ofReal(1−0)=1 by the restriction definition and M011; thus ν is finite and ν([0,1])=1. Integrate by M009 and use M002 to interchange the ℕ-indexed sum and lintegral; countability and AEMeasurability have just been checked. By M010 each summand integral equals ρᵢ^sν(Jᵢ∩[0,1]). For S=Jᵢ∩[0,1], the restriction definition gives ν(S)=volume(S∩[0,1])=volume(S). Choose a closed interval containing S (if S is empty choose any such interval) with endpoints ordered and length ≤ρᵢ+ηᵢ. M013 gives volume(S)≤volume of that closed interval, and M011 evaluates the latter as ofReal(length)≤ofReal(ρᵢ+ηᵢ). Thus C_s(E,δ)≤∑'ᵢρᵢ^(s+1)+∑'ᵢηᵢρᵢ^s≤∑'ᵢρᵢ^(s+1)+ε because ηᵢρᵢ^s≤ε2^(−i−1) and ∑ᵢ2^(−i−1)=1. For the fixed cover, ε is arbitrary: if its (s+1)-cost is finite, ε↓0 gives C_s(E,δ)≤that cost; if infinite the inequality is immediate. Taking the infimum over all covers gives C_s(E,δ)≤C_(s+1)(F,δ). As δ decreases to zero the left side diverges, so the right side diverges; M008 gives H^(s+1)(F)=∞. Apply M001 with NNReal exponent s+1 to obtain s+1≤dim_H(F). This holds for every 0<s<D, so density implies D+1≤dim_H(F). Use NNReal coercions for dimension theorems and the corresponding real exponents in M008.
